* **The checkout says which remote is public, not the environment.** The
  remotes read and the reachability read both run with git's
  repository-selection and injected-config variables removed (`GIT_DIR`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and its pairs, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, and the rest
  that `vcs._authority_env` names). An ambient value therefore cannot
  pair a public URL with the private origin's refs. A remote counts only
  when the checkout's own config gives it one GitHub repository. A URL
  set in the global or system config, or two different URLs on one
  remote, count for nothing, and the refusal names that remote. gh is
  asked `github.com/<owner/name>`, so `GH_HOST` cannot answer for it.
  Only a plain GitHub repository URL (https, ssh or scp form, owner and
  name and nothing more) names a repository. A URL with a `#` or a `?`
  before the `@`, a dot segment, or a `file://` scheme only looks like a
  GitHub URL, because git takes it to another host, repository or path.
  It names no repository, here and on the owner's board.
* **A rewriting release shares no commit.** helm's export is a line of
  release commits, each a NEW commit whose tree is the trunk tree minus
  the omit list, so no development commit is ever on the public remote.
  Every helm lane and trunk tip is therefore refused for an or-free
  seat. That is correct, because the trunk tree holds the omitted paths.
  The public code such a seat may read is the release commit itself
  (`aspublic/main`), never the private commit it was built from.
* **Only a fresh answer admits.** The visibility is gh's answer, kept for
  a day, and only the remotes that hold the tip are asked about. When
  none of them has a fresh PUBLIC answer, a missing or day-old answer is
  asked again and the dispatch waits for it, up to 20 s. A day-old
  `public` does not admit, and a failed ask refuses the row for an hour.
  A recipient on any other route is admitted with no git call and no gh
  call.
* **Its window is 168000**: the router's listed 200000 less the family's
  32000 output cap.
* **Some free models are also fleet models.** The router's pool on the
  ruling's day listed `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free` (the same base model as the
  `qwen27` seat), `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free` (the `dots3` seat)
  and `cohere/north-mini-code:free` (`or-code`). The ruling treats the class
  as distinct from all of them; the transcript is where a reader checks which
  model served a given read.

**Every local window leaves a compaction margin.** For each family served
from the operator's own box, every window the launch line teaches, plus the
output cap it sends, plus `LOCAL_COMPACTION_MARGIN` (16384, a floor), must fit
the server slot (`probed_context_length`). The catalog refuses to import a
local family that breaks this, and `helm seat doctor` flags a minted local
seat whose effective window breaks it (a `settings.json` `env` pin outranks
the launch stamp), with a non-zero exit. The reason is measured: a
`qwenlocal` seat taught 229376 beside a 32768 output cap filled its 262144
server maximum exactly. One large tool result took a request to 262145 and
the server refused it. The compaction call carried the same context and was
refused too, so the seat stayed wedged until a `/clear`. With the margin,
the server still has room when the context reaches the taught window. The
floor holds one Bash result (30000 characters inline) and the compaction
instruction. It does not hold a full Read or MCP result (25000 tokens each),
so a family that reads large files keeps more: `qwenlocal` keeps 32768,
`qwen27` keeps 17152 through its budget, and `bonsai` keeps the floor.

**The lite launch profile.** A family whose seats run on a small window, or
whose every tool schema is prefill on the operator's own GPU, declares
`"profile": "lite"` (task/3253). Today the three local families do: `qwen27`,
`qwenlocal` and `bonsai`. One table, `seat_catalog.PROFILES`, says what the
profile means, and every surface reads its switch from there:

* **Four more tools leave both deny surfaces**: `Workflow`, `SendMessage`,
  `ListAgents` and `WebFetch` (`seat_catalog.LITE_UNUSED_TOOLS`). Measured
  on 2026-09-26 with each local seat's real config and the served model's own
  tokenizer: a request's fixed cost was about 14,570 tokens, `Workflow`'s
  schema alone was 5,818 of it (40 %), and in 5,177 recorded tool calls the
  local seats called none of the four.
* **`Workflow`, reconciled with task/2559.** That ruling keeps a capped
  `Workflow` on a proxy seat because it is how a seat delegates to another
  model of its own family. A lite family that declares a same-family delegate
  tier (`subagent_tiers`) keeps the capped tool on exactly that ground. A lite
  family that declares none has no second model to delegate to, so the tool
  is denied, and its launch line and `settings.json` carry no workflow cap.
* **The MCP floor** (`exa`) only, wherever the family is served.
* **The window pins.** The seat's `settings.json` `env` carries the window
  (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`) and
  the output cap (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) that the launch line
  stamps, plus the family's `lite_env`. A pin there outranks the launch
  stamp, so helm writes it from the stamp's own number. **A re-seed never
  raises an operator's pin**: helm's record (`helm.seeded_env`) maps each
  pin helm wrote to the value it wrote, and only a pin still at that value
  is helm's and follows the catalog both ways. Any other pin is the
  operator's: one below the catalog (the hot-fix for a catalog that is
  stale-high after a server shrinks its slot) is kept by every `seat
  resume`, and one above it is lowered, the safe direction. This holds for
  the window knobs and every output cap alike. `bonsai`'s `lite_env`
  caps a Read and an MCP result at 8000 tokens and a Bash result at 20000
  characters, so one tool result fits the compaction margin its window keeps.
* **The operator's rule files stay out.** `claudeMdExcludes` names the
  default home's `CLAUDE.md` (and the file the seat's `rules/` link points
  at, when that is another) and, when the seat's cwd is known (`seat spawn`
  and `seat resume`), `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`
  in every directory above the cwd's git top level. The project's own rules
  still load. Nothing here is a literal path: every entry derives from the
  home, the configured instructions source or the cwd.

The `settings.json` entries are seeded like the deny list: added on every
`seat add`, `launch`, `spawn` and `resume`, never removed, and each one helm
wrote is recorded under the `helm` key (`seeded_env`, `seeded_excludes`) so a
later change can retire it. `helm seat doctor` prints one row per minted
lite seat: `profile lite: <seat> OK`, or `DRIFT` naming what differs between
the seat's live `settings.json` and `.claude.json` and the catalog (a missing
deny, an env pin a resume would rewrite, a missing exclude, an MCP server
above the floor), which fails the exit status. An operator's pin below the
catalog is named on its own line and does not fail it (`OK, operator pin
X=N below the catalog M kept; lower the catalog if it is right`): a resume
keeps it, so the cure is the catalog, not the seat. A file that cannot be
parsed reads `UNKNOWN` and does not. `helm seat resume <seat>` re-seeds the
settings; an MCP server comes out by hand.

**A tool a route cannot serve is denied where its failure was measured.**
Claude Code's `WebSearch` asks the upstream to run a server search tool.
One probe per family on 2026-09-26 found it failing on `qwen27`, `qwenlocal`,
`bonsai`, `ds4pro`, `gptoss`, `opus46` and `cursor` (on the local seats
silently: no links, then an instruction to cite sources, which invites
invented ones), and working on native claude seats, on the codex models and
on `gemini`. Each of the seven declares `unserved_tools` and launches without
`WebSearch` (task/3242); `kimi` and `grok` are unmeasured and keep it. The
local families also launch without `ExitPlanMode`: on 2026-09-25 their seats
made 77 calls to it, one loop of "You are not in plan mode" refusals.

**`opus46` and `gptoss` — two seats on ONE credential and ONE quota group.**
Both ride the same Antigravity OAuth file the `gemini` seat rides (mode
"proxy-oauth", channel `antigravity`), on ports 8346 and 8348. What makes them
separate seats rather than gemini fallbacks is that the account meters TWO
allowances: the Gemini models bill one weekly/5-hour group and the Claude and
GPT models bill another. On 2026-09-18 the Gemini group read 0 percent
remaining until about Sep 22 while the other read 100 percent, on the identical
credential — so the gemini seat was walled and these two answered.

* **`opus46` runs `claude-opus-4-6-thinking`; `gptoss` runs
  `gpt-oss-120b-medium`.** One model, one seat name: a fallback that changed
  the model under a name would break the only thing a review's authority is a
  claim about. Re-measured through the live proxy, one 8-token completion each:
  200 in 2.79s and 200 in 1.76s, non-empty text on both.
* **The Claude seat is an OWNER EXCEPTION scoped to this subscription.** Claude
  models otherwise run only through Claude Code on the owner's Max credential.
  The allotment here is Google's, bought with the Antigravity plan, and no
  Anthropic API key or SDK appears anywhere in the path. The exception is about
  the CREDENTIAL, not about the model name.
* **The credential is SHARED BY COPY.** Each family declares
  `shares_credential_with: gemini`, and `helm seat add` copies the sibling's
  antigravity auth file into this seat's own auth-dir at 0600 when the seat has
  none and no `--auth-from` was given. It is a copy and not a shared directory
  because the proxy rewrites its auth file at every token refresh, so two
  proxies on one directory would be two writers on one file. An explicit
  `--auth-from` still wins; a source credential that cannot authenticate is
  refused rather than copied.
* **Both bill the `antigravity-claude-gpt` group, and `helm seat where` says
  so.** The line names the group and who shares it, and reports the remaining
  percent as `not yet measured` until something reads the vendor's quota
  endpoint (task/2800). It never renders a default percent: a plausible number
  in that slot is one an owner acts on.
* **Both are findings-only.** Neither family key is among the approval-tier
  policy's members, and a verdict records the author's FAMILY KEY as its
  resolved family — so an approve minted on either resolves `outside` by the
  same closed-set check that refuses every other outsider. `gptoss` is a NEW
  family and therefore a true cross-family read for both claude- and
  codex-authored work once it passes the known-defect bar; `opus46` resolves to
  a Claude MODEL on a non-native family key, which is task/2802's subject and
  is not loosened here.

A seat is a **first-class fleet chat member and dregg identity**. `seat launch`
exports `HELM_CHAT_NAME=<family>` (keeping the existing
`env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` scrub), so the seat's SessionStart join registers it
in the roster under its family name and `@codex` / `@kimi` fleet posts deliver
to it between tool calls. The same line exports the dregg-native signer
(`HELM_CELL_BIN=~/.local/bin/dregg-client-sign`) plus
`HELM_CELL_PROFILE=<family>` and `DREGG_PROFILE=<family>`: the first signed post
creates the named SDK profile and faucet-materializes its own cell, so agent
activity advances the cave as that seat — never through an inherited owner
profile. The delivery lane (deliver + subagent-end + join) lives in the seat's `claude/`
config dir; `helm hooks install` wires it there and `helm hooks status` reports
seat coverage (see `helm hooks`). A seat already running an OLD session must be
relaunched with a fresh `helm seat launch` to pick up the identity, signer, and
delivery hooks — a live session's environment/settings are fixed at start.

`seat add` and `seat launch` also derive the current project room by default;
`--room` and an inherited explicit `HELM_CHAT_ROOM` win. Generated `launch.sh`
presets preserve `HELM_CHAT_ROOM_SOURCE=derived` across `helm seat resume`, so a
refresh cannot turn a project default into an explicit room and undo a later
operator rehome/clear. Resume also preserves the seat's `--multi` shape and
refreshes `spawn.json` with the new pane handle.

**`helm seat resume <seat>` brings the seat back EXACTLY AS IT RAN**
(task/3695). It used to re-mint a proxy seat's launch from today's catalog and
resume an orca-adopted lead with no `--model` and no permission flag, so every
parked seat came back on whatever the defaults were that day: measured
2026-09-29, helm-codex (running gpt-6-sol after a `/model`, window 320000)
would have come back at the catalog's 220000, and meta-claude (running
claude-opus-5-5[1m] in bypassPermissions after a `/model` over its
`--model fable` argv) on its home's `opus[1m]` and `auto` mode. The resume now
carries the seat's LAUNCH RECIPE (`helm/seat_recipe.py`): model, credential
home, cwd, permission mode, effort (the level; a recorded ultracode is shown
and no resume restores it, and the plan says so), denied tools, appended
system prompt and identity environment, and for a proxy seat its family,
window and subagent pin. Each field is read from the first source that states
it: the session's own transcript for what moves while it runs (Claude Code's
`model` attachment carries the exact id, and a later `/model` is honoured; the
last permission mode; the effort level), then the seat's live process
(`/proc` argv cut to the recipe's own words and an ALLOW-LISTED environ — no
bearer, and no --settings env block or --mcp-config header an adopted lead's
argv carries, is ever kept. EVERY FIELD PASSES AN ALLOW-LIST: a flag's
value must be a model the seat catalog knows, a mode or effort level claude's
flag takes, a tool name Claude Code ships or a deny rule helm's catalog mints,
a catalog system line, or the ultracode boolean; an environment value must be
a seat name by helm's seat-name rule, a home under ~/.claude, ~/.claude-homes
or helm's own home, a catalogued family, a window or a catalogued model; the
binary is kept only as the version its versions layout names. A value outside
its list, such as the text of an adopted lead's --append-system-prompt or a
token passed as --model, is never stored, carried, printed or logged: its
field reads unknown by name. A config dir is kept only when it IS a home helm
knows (exactly ~/.claude or helm's home, a seat home helm minted, or a named
credhome that exists under ~/.claude-homes), never for lying under one; a
version only as plain N.N.N. The ASSEMBLED recipe is checked the same way
whatever the source, the transcript's facts included, and a model is named
only when the catalog or an alias knows it or it is in Claude's own id
grammar, so a retired Claude id is still named and anything else is "a model
the catalog does not know"), then the capture every `seat resume --all --apply` pass keeps of each LIVE seat in the
resume live set's `recipes` map (carried forward pass to pass and boot to
boot, and read only for a session its process held), then a proxy seat's
launch.sh. A proxy seat's launch.sh is re-minted to carry the recipe, and its
effort rides the pane command as `--effort`; an adopted lead's resume script
carries the flags and exports (unsetting what it ran without).

**EXACTLY means one launch.** The transcript is the session's own record, and
a live process or a capture is a process that held the session, so their
fields are one launch's recipe. launch.sh is bound to no launch: `seat
remint`, `seat launch` and `seat add` rewrite it with no launch after it. So a
recipe that reads launch.sh beside a field the transcript states (the model it
ran beside a re-minted window) is not one launch's: those launch.sh fields are
unknown, each named with its source (`window [last launch (launch.sh)]`), and
the resume refuses as it does for any unknown field. A seat the reboot sweep
captured while it ran resumes exactly after a re-mint; one it never captured
resumes on `--defaults`. A cv-pruned copy is the same conversation under a
new session id: its own lineage stamp names the session it was pruned from,
and the capture of the process that held that session binds the copy, so a
captured seat's context-wall recovery resumes the copy exactly.

**A capture binds a resume only as this session's LAST launch.** Same
session (its process held it), same process birth (pid and start stamp, and
the process the spawn register pins to the session, where it pins one), and
no launch of the seat of any kind recorded after it was taken; for a pruned
copy, a lineage stamp naming exactly the source the resume asked for.
**THE LAUNCH RECORD** (`seat-launches.jsonl` in helm's global dir) is written
by helm's SessionStart hook (`seat resume-turn --hook-json`, which every helm
home runs in every project) once for each process start of a session:
`startup`, `resume` (`--resume`, `--continue`, an in-session `/resume`, Orca's
own relaunch, a hand `claude --resume`) and `fork`, and `clear` when it
carries the same process's capture; `compact` keeps the session in the same
process and writes none, and neither does a `claude -p` helper, which is not
the seat. Each row is `{session, seat, home, model,
source, ts, capture}`, and `capture` is the capture of the process that
started (the `CLAUDE_PID` Claude Code gives its hooks), so a row exists only
for a launch that really started and IS its freshest capture: the newest row
for a session is what its resume binds, unless the sweep captured a process
after it (a later start whose hook wrote nothing), which then binds instead;
a row whose process could not be read binds nothing unless such a capture
follows it. A `seat rehome` ledger row or an adopted resume's script newer
than the newest row is a later launch that can only unbind (a rehome row
naming the process that row captured is that launch). The reboot sweep's
capture is the fallback for a session no row names (one started before the
record existed), bound against the spawn register's stamp and those older
records. The hook never
fails a session: it waits on the record's lock at most a second, and a row it
cannot write leaves a marker (`seat-launches.unrecorded/<sid>`) that reads as
an unread record, so nothing binds that session's next resume; a record that
does not read binds nothing, and the note names it. A live process speaks only
for the session it holds, so `--session OLD` never borrows the recipe of the
process running NEW. Anything short of that reads as uncaptured, and the
recipe's notes say which rule it failed. A launch on a home without helm's
hooks leaves no row and cannot be seen.

**No resume changes the account a seat is paid by, or the model it ran,
unseen.** A known account mismatch refuses on every path, `--defaults` and an
unattended caller included, except for a seat whose captured launch ran on
the default home (`~/.claude`) and resumes there: its payer is whichever
account Orca holds, and Orca switching it is the fleet's designed wall
handling, so there the resume prints `account: <now> now; it ran on <then>`
and goes on. An adopted lead's last recorded launch names the home
it ran on, over the session-creds index (which keeps the first home it saw);
an unattended caller whose fallback would move it off that home leaves it down
naming the home, and `--defaults` prints the move. An unattended caller that
would change the model the recipe knows the seat ran leaves it down instead,
in one line naming why; the operator's `--defaults` prints that change and
takes it. A reply names a model without its 1M suffix: after `/model
<id>[1m]` (or `opus[1m]`) the argument restores it, a launch's `--model
opus[1m]` restores it for a reply alone, and a `/model` menu pick or a typed
alias without the suffix (`/model default`, `/model opus`) answered by a
Claude id leaves the model unknown (`seat recipe` says why), so the resume
refuses it by name. The window
an exact resume stamps reaches the process: a lite seat's settings.json pin,
which outranks the launch stamp, is seeded from the recipe's window, and a
pin the re-seed would keep at another value refuses the resume, naming the
knob. An orca-adopted seat whose session lives in a proxy seat's tree is
planned by the same rules, and resumes through that seat's own launch.sh
with the model and effort it ran.

**An unattended resume never leaves a seat down.** The reboot sweep and the
context-wall recovery have no operator to choose `--defaults`. When every
field a recipe lacks is one a defaults resume never takes from the seat's
past run (every field but the session's cwd and an adopted lead's
credential home), they resume on today's defaults and print one line,
`WARNING: <the reboot sweep|the context-wall recovery> resumes it on TODAY'S
defaults, not the recipe it ran with: <fields> unknown, …`, before the
fields that move, except where that would change the account or the model
it ran (above). The operator's `helm seat resume` refuses the same recipe.

**A resume never silently swaps a model, an account or a permission mode.** A
recipe with a field no source knows REFUSES before anything is stopped or
written, and names the fields (`saved only: disallowed_tools, … unknown`),
a field a source set outside its allow-list included (a permission mode or
effort level claude's own flag does not take among them), never its value; so
does one the launch line cannot carry (a model the family no longer
catalogues, a proxy seat that ran outside bypassPermissions), and an adopted
lead whose home now holds a different account than the one it held when the
lead's process was captured. The account check compares one kind of id on
both sides, the measured key of the account email a home holds (never the
address, and never the transcript's bridge-session id, which is another kind
of id); a side it cannot read prints `account: UNKNOWN (<why>)` and refuses
nothing. `--defaults` is the explicit choice of today's defaults, the old
behaviour: it prints each field that moves (`model gpt-5.6-sol -> gpt-6-sol`,
`window 320000 -> 220000`, `UNKNOWN -> …` for a field the recipe lacked) and
then resumes. A proxy seat whose recorded window is larger than the one the
catalog teaches for its model resumes with the window it ran, and says so.

**Identity follows the roster.** One field of a proxy seat's recipe comes from
the roster, not from the launch it ran: its identity. HELM_CHAT_NAME,
HELM_CELL_PROFILE and DREGG_PROFILE are derived from the roster at every
launch, and a durable `helm chat seat rename` is the operator changing them
on purpose. So a renamed proxy seat resumes under the roster's new name, prints
`identity follows the roster: <recorded> -> <roster>`, and is never refused
for it; every other field resumes as it ran.

### `helm seat recipe <seat> [--json]`

READ-ONLY. The launch recipe a seat runs (or ran) with, one line per field
with its value and source, the recorded-only fields (harness version, paying
account), and the answer the Asleep / Saved-only states read:
`resume: resumes exactly`, or `resume: saved only: <fields> unknown`. The last
line is what `seat resume <seat> --defaults` would change, field by field.
`--json` prints the same as one object. An adopted seat whose recorded role
is lead gets one more line (`lead_posture` in `--json`) naming the lead
posture its resume adds; the readout writes nothing to say so. Exit 1 when the
recipe is incomplete (a seat whose resume would refuse), 0 otherwise, 2 for an
unknown seat.

**`helm seat resume <seat>` resumes the session the seat's LIVE process holds,
not the newest transcript** (task/3208). Measured twice on a fleet host: a
`/clear`, then a resume at once, came back on the pre-clear session at 85%.
The process's presence record (`<config>/sessions/<pid>.json`) names the new
session the instant `/clear` lands, while the transcripts lag it — the new
session has none yet on a claude that writes it lazily, or (claude 2.1.283)
one holding only the `/clear` records and no assistant turn, which the
reboot-stub ranking puts below the old session's real turns. So a hand resume
reads the live record first (`seat_lifecycle_runtime.live_seat_session`): one
live session is resumed with `--resume`, or with `--session-id` when it has no
transcript yet (claude refuses `--resume` for that and accepts `--session-id`,
both measured, and `--continue` would take the old session again) — the resume
says so, and asks again after the reap in case the session wrote its first
transcript in between. A live record speaks for the seat only on the spawn
register's evidence: its session is the register's, or the register pins that
exact pid and birth stamp, or the register holds no session and the record is
the seat's interactive claude (entrypoint `cli`, the rule `seat rehome` uses).
A `claude -p` helper the seat started writes a record of its own session in
the same home (entrypoint `sdk-cli`) and can outlive the seat's claude, so a
record with none of that evidence is a helper's, the resume says so, and the
ranking decides (the price: a `/clear`
whose SessionStart bind the register refused resumes the old session, as it
did before). A pruned copy of the live session still outranks it, as the
rescue. Admitted records naming different sessions that the register's pin
cannot choose between, or records that cannot be read, REFUSE before anything
is reaped. With no live process — the record of a dead pid names nothing — the
newest-transcript ranking decides, as before;
the pins (`--session`, the reboot sweep, the CONTEXT_FULL recovery) name their
session already and never read it. `helm seat autocompact` reads its context
gauge from the same live session's transcript, so a cleared seat is never
measured by the session it left.

**`helm seat idle-dispatch [--dry-run] [--apply] [--quiet] [--json]` — the
stranded-obligation rung.** One pass crosses every open dispatch row against
its recipient's presence and the recipient's own claims, looked up by holder.
Each row it finds is reported: one line per row on the console, and every
fact (claim state, held leases, context pressure, pane and wall readings,
wake route) under `--json`, with the sender's decision as `sender_act`. The
dispatch's sender gets a DM only when it has a decision to make:

| State | Meaning | Sender DM |
|---|---|---|
| STRANDED | quiet, holds no live claim, no measured live pane | yes: re-check or reassign |
| CLAIM-UNKNOWN | the claims ledger could not be read, or a live claim names no holder | yes: read the ledger; never reassign on an unread fact |
| WORKING | quiet and holds no claim, but the pane is measurably live | only when no beacon is armed, at first sight and again every 4h while the row stays open: tend the pane, or reassign a pane that cannot be tended. With an armed beacon, no: the report line says `no DM` |
| HOLDING | quiet and holds a live claim | no: the report line says `no DM` |

The act a WORKING row needs is a wake to the recipient. When a beacon is
armed, the second leg sends that wake and the sender has nothing to do. When
none is, a DM cannot reach the pane and nobody else will act on it, so the
sender is told. It is told again every 4h (the backoff cap) while the row
stays open and unwakeable, so a stuck row never goes silent. A HOLDING owner
is never reassigned. Some of its wedges have their own watchdogs (autocompact
for a full context window, the prompt-stall watch, proxywatch for a provider
wall). A holder that is live and idle, not at a prompt, not near a full
context window and not walled, has no watchdog until its lease expires, and
`--ttl` has no upper bound. When the lease expires, the row reads STRANDED,
or WORKING on a measured live pane.

The latch keys on the sender's decision, and each decision's record lives as
long as the row is open, in any state. STRANDED and CLAIM-UNKNOWN repeat on
the doubling backoff, and the WORKING DM repeats on a fixed 4h cadence. A
flap between states keeps each record and its backoff count or cadence, so a
return to a decision already told is not told again until its wait expires,
and WORKING -> HOLDING -> WORKING on a wakeable recipient sends nothing. Each
record names the custodian it told, so when custody of a row moves, the new
custodian is told at once. The second leg DMs the recipient of a row that
holds no claim (STRANDED or WORKING), only when a beacon is measured armed
and no provider wall is read. `--dry-run` and `--quiet` report without
sending or changing latch state.

IDLE-OWING (task/3118). A beacon beats a seat's presence on every poll, so a
beaconed seat reads `fresh` and its rows used to be dropped as busy whether
the seat was working or asleep at its prompt. The rung now also reads the
seat's own hooks (`helm/seat_idle.py`): the last tool call, the last turn
start and the last turn end the stop-guard door answered with rc 0, all
kept in the session's recorder file. A seat whose turn ended and which has
run nothing since is IDLE; a call or turn start after the turn end is BUSY;
anything unreadable is UNKNOWN, and a resting seat is RESTING, so neither is
ever IDLE. A row whose recipient has been IDLE ten minutes or more while
owing it is IDLE-OWING whatever its presence. With an armed beacon and no
provider wall, the seat is rung: one DM naming the row and
`helm dispatch triage <id>`. The sender is not told, because the ring is the
act, and the second leg does not wake the same row. The ring's record lives
as long as the row is open, so it repeats only on the doubling backoff, across
idle episodes. Every sending pass appends one sample per owing seat to
`<helm home>/_global/.state/idle-owing.jsonl`.

THE DARK-SEAT MOVER (task/3587). Every pass also judges, for each seat that
owes a row or a task, whether anything can reach it. A seat is DARK when
`helm burn` reads its family RED on MONEY or REACH (a vendor quota wall, an
upstream outage, or a billing or credential refusal on a seat's own last
turn), when its own last turn ended on such a refusal, or when the usability
join measures its pane GONE with no armed beacon, so nothing can deliver a
row or wake it. A seat whose pane is live but whose beacon is not is DEAF,
not dark: the beacons census asks it to re-arm and `helm seat resume-turn
--nudge --seat S` wakes it now, so it keeps its rows and the pass says that
once. A seat the remote relay drives is never judged here: its liveness is
its relay session, read by the same predicate the sweep above uses, and a
row the relay cannot account for moves nothing. A seat or family read dark
on every pass for `HELM_DARK_MOVE_GRACE_S` (default ten minutes, latched in
`<helm home>/_global/.state/dark_move.json`) is confirmed, and its work
moves to live seats. Unstarted work is an OPEN
dispatch row whose recipient holds neither a claim on the row nor the
dispatched lane's lease (`progress_state` IDLE), holds no room of the lane's
family (the room fence `dispatch rebind` warns of), and, for any row but a
review, whose lane branches carry no commits on neither trunk nor the
dispatched ref; and a task that is `open` with an owner (`helm task claim`
sets `in_progress`, so the owner never claimed it) whose owner holds no live
lease on a lane whose name carries the task's number anywhere (`task-N`,
`<slug>-N`, `<slug>-Nr`) or that the task records as a `lane:<name>` ref, and
whose such lane branches in this helm's repository carry no commits off
trunk. Started work moves too (task/3881), unless the wall's known reset is
within `HELM_DARK_MOVE_RESET_WAIT_S` (an hour): a task `in_progress`, or
`open` with such a lease or lane commits. The pass reads every room git has
checked out on one of the task's lanes. When no room holds an uncommitted
change (`git status --porcelain`: tracked changes and untracked files count,
ignored files do not, and a merge or rebase in progress counts), the task's
own leases move to the target (rolled back if the owner move is refused),
then its owner through the seat-reassign capability (its status stays), then
the dark seat's working dispatch rows on the same lanes through `dispatch
rebind`. No force is used: a running owner still refuses the move, unless
its liveness reads WALLED or BLOCKED_ON_QUOTA with its reset more than an
hour away (`helm seat reassign`'s WALLED disposition), and the task's
reassign record names that classification and its reset. The receiving seat gets one DM naming the task, each lane, its room
and tip: continue from this tip, since the commits on the lane are the dark
seat's finished work; review and land them, then finish the task. When a
room is dirty nothing moves, and one #seats row @mentions the integrator
with the seat, the task, the room and the dirty paths, once until that
changes. Started tasks move first, P0, then P1, then the rest. Each kept row
prints why it stays. A
review goes to a measured-eligible reader `helm reviewers` names, which
already refuses every seat that wrote a round of the chain (a cure's patch
author included) and a seat outside the approval tier; the review needs one
approval-tier read by a non-author, so no other family is required. Any other
row goes to a seat the usability join measures USABLE, not held, storming or
walled, whose family a fresh burn snapshot names, and a task or build row
whose project has an authored team (`helm team`) only to a member of it (a
row's project is its repository's). Among the candidates the seat owing the fewest open rows and
tasks is taken, counting the pass's own moves. A dark seat, or a seat of a
dark family, is never a target. It is DRY-RUN unless `--apply`, and
`--dry-run` wins: the pass prints what it would move. With `--apply`, a row
moves through `dispatch rebind` (the cancelled row's reason names the dark
family, and the successor carries the brief; a room the old seat still holds
is named on the move line and the post), a task through the seat-reassign
capability, which a measurably LIVE owner refuses (no force overrides it:
the task stays and the refusal is printed), and each move posts one line in
#helm. A row moves at most once
per pass, and a pass makes at most `HELM_DARK_MOVE_MAX` (5) moves; the rest
wait for the next pass, and the pass says how many. A row with no live
eligible seat stays where it is and is reported once, until it moves or its
seat comes back; a dry pass latches that apart from an `--apply` pass, so
the first `--apply` pass still posts it. An unreadable roster, dispatch,
claims or task ledger, lane refs git cannot count, a task of another
project's repository, or a project team that does not read moves nothing and
says so in one line; with no fresh burn snapshot nothing moves at all, since
no target's family is known to spend. The
shipped timer runs the pass without `--apply`, so the owner turns the mover
on by adding it to `helm-idle-dispatch.service`.

`helm seat idle-dispatch --owing [--hours H] [--json]` reads those samples over
the last H hours (default 2) and answers the two idle bars directly: per seat,
the minutes it sat IDLE while owing a row, each stretch over ten minutes, and
whether a pass inside the stretch rang it. The minutes run to the last pass
that saw the stretch, so they are a lower bound by up to one pass interval,
and the header names the largest gap between passes. No pass in the window
prints UNKNOWN and exits 1.

`helm seat where <seat>` prints the same reading beside the pane's liveness
(`hooks IDLE 25m (turn ended 18:00Z, nothing run since)`), and
`helm dispatch list` marks an owed row IDLE-OWING, or names the recipient's
reading on a late row that is not.

**`helm seat autocompact` — pre-empt the proxy-model 100% context hang.** One
bounded pass reads Claude Code's own latest main-chain usage record from every
proxy seat transcript, divides by that family's declared context window, and
at 80% injects `/compact` into the identity-proven pane. A main-chain
`compact_boundary` newer than that usage record is the reading instead: its
`compactMetadata.postTokens` when that is a positive count, else UNKNOWN, and
never the usage from before the compaction (task/3534). The actuator uses the
seat's authoritative `spawn.json` handle and verifies it against the matching
adapter's live inventory. The same resolver owns duplicate-seat reap and
`seat where`; copied launch text and mutable pane titles are never identity.
Missing/headless/stale-register panes produce a loud room alert instead of a
guessed injection. Before sending, the actuator proves the current composer. An
exact pretyped `/compact` outside an open turn authorizes Enter only (never a
duplicate retype); `RUNNING` still refuses because submitted-message history uses
the same prompt glyph. Arguments and every other non-empty draft remain
untouched. An empty composer in `CONTEXT_FULL` may receive the normal `/compact`
injection because compaction is
that state's remedy. Adapter success alone is not actuation: bounded pane rereads
must prove the command drained or the pane transitioned before a locked success
latch is written. A static composer, or a send the adapter refused, is reported
as FAILED_TO_SUBMIT and retried next cadence. Verified actuation permits one fire per context episode
and re-arms only after context drops or the authoritative registered session
changes; elapsed time and a newer transcript alone never release the latch.
A pane that ANSWERS `/compact` with one of Claude Code's own refusals ("Not
enough messages to compact", no messages, a blocking PreCompact hook, a failed,
cancelled or skipped compaction) gets no further `/compact` until it has a
usage reading newer than the refusal; a changed session or pane identity does
not re-arm it. The answer is read in the post-send rereads and again off the
screen before the next send, and the refusal is said once (task/3534). A send
whose effect helm cannot prove (the bytes went in, and no drain, no turn and no
refusal followed) is latched the same way, fail closed, and is said once too.

A refusal alarm keyed to an episode the seat can no longer be read as (a new
session or pane) could never meet its same-episode discharge. It is discharged
when the seat's newest reading is measured on its own session, below the
alarm's threshold, and newer than the start of the alarm's run; the discharge
line carries a `STALE EPISODE` trace naming both keys and both times.

An already-full seat takes a separate, fail-closed rung. Recovery requires
either repeated line-leading context-overflow 400s or a newly caused post-send
400 whose exact fingerprint remains above its pre-send count on the next cadence;
proxywatch `HUNG`, silence, historical errors, and generic HTTP 400s cannot act.
Helm asks `cv prune --window … --drop-thinking --json` (`--thinking` on cv
0.10) to mint a bounded copy with
revive enabled, independently verifies that copy's recorded context fits the
budget, and resumes that exact id in the prior registered worktree. Success is
published only after the replacement pane is live and the seat's claim-session
bindings have moved without changing their lease nonce, fence, or expiry.
`/clear` is the last resort only when pruning cannot create a copy. Once a copy
exists, validation or relaunch failure preserves both sessions, latches the
episode for manual recovery, and never falls through to `/clear`.

**A limited family can declare a context budget and a fresh session between
rows (task/2944).** Every request re-sends the whole context, so for a family
with a limited allowance the context size is the spend rate. kimi's weekly
allowance went in about 30 hours: one long-lived session carried many rows, so
a typical request carried 329k tokens. Two `helm/seat_catalog.py` fields fix
this:

- `context_budget` narrows the window a seat is taught. The launch line puts it
  on both CC knobs and this watchdog reads the same number
  (`seat_catalog.taught_window`). `max_context` keeps the model's measured
  window and its evidence. A budget can only narrow: one at or above
  `max_context`, or on a family with no `max_context`, refuses at import.
  kimi is taught 380000 and compacts at 304k. The number is sized from the
  p95 per-row peak (`KIMI_ROW_PEAK_P95`, 300,373 tokens over 174 rows replayed
  under the rung below), so about 95% of rows finish without compacting. A
  200k budget would compact about one row in five, which is the "compacted
  about 5x too often" complaint that set kimi's 1M window.
- `fresh_session_floor` starts a fresh session BETWEEN rows. A seat of that
  family is cleared when all of these are true: it carries at least the floor
  (kimi: 100000), its transcript is quiet for 5 minutes, its pane is IDLE with
  an empty composer, no owed dispatch row names it under any alias, and it
  holds no live claim. The rung uses the `/clear` and onboarding rungs above
  without change, so the new session re-arms its beacon and reads
  `helm dispatch list --mine --open` before its next row. It clears between
  rows, never when a row arrives, because the beacon wakes the seat on a new
  row in seconds. An unreadable ledger, a claim with no holder, an open turn
  or a draft refuses. One clear per seat per 15 minutes bounds the cost if the
  onboarding alone crosses the floor. The routine clear and onboarding post
  nothing; a seat that was cleared but not re-briefed posts a loud alert,
  because its beacon is not armed. `--dry-run` shows `would start a fresh
  session`. The budget reaches a seat at its next launch; the between-rows rung
  runs on the next watchdog pass.

**A budget also stops a seat that goes quiet below its model's window
(task/3085).** gemini is taught 500000 of its 1M window and compacts at 400k.
Its seat stopped working at about 634k: it answered three beacon wakes with
"Standing by." and did not take the row it owed. The model can hold more (two
native compactions at 784k succeeded) and no request failed, so against the
taught 1M that stall read 63.4% and nothing fired. `GEMINI_STALL` records the
reading; the budget sits under it, and its compaction point sits above the
family's observed floor.

**Every alarm names its window and the window's source.** The /compact line,
the refusal and CANNOT ACT lines, the dead and backstop lines and the WATCHDOG
refusal-loop line all say `its N-token window (source: S)`, where S is
`FAMILIES.model_context[<model>]`, `FAMILIES.max_context`,
`FAMILIES.context_budget`, `HELM_AUTOCOMPACT_ASSUME_WINDOW` (a window the
operator declared for this host) or `cc-assumed-default` (CC's own 200k for a
non-claude model, which is what an unpinned family is taught). The text row
shows the same source in brackets.

**Nothing fires on an unproven window (task/3534).** A reading against
`cc-assumed-default` is shown and never acted on: the row's status is
`window-unproven` and the text row says `window unproven, no fire`. Over the
trigger it posts one REPORT-ONLY line per 5 points of climb. The owner's
ruling: "really bad practice to make auto-firing things that we dont fully
understand the input data about". To make such a seat fire, declare the
family's window in `seat_catalog.FAMILIES` with its evidence, or set
`HELM_AUTOCOMPACT_ASSUME_WINDOW=<tokens>` to declare one for the host.
Proxywatch, reviewer ranking and route read such a seat's context as
UNKNOWN, keyed on where the window came from, so a row gone `stale` is
UNKNOWN too. That rules out only `compact-needed`: it is not an unread
input, so a seat whose other inputs are measured still reads `hung` (not
routable) or `idle`.

**The window is the served model's, not the family's.** A reading is divided
by the window its launch line teaches for the model that served it: the model
the usage record names, else the seat's registered `--model`, else its
declared instance model (`seat_catalog.launch_window`). A codex seat on
gpt-5.6-sol reads against 320,000, not the family default's 220,000; read
against 220,000, 231,746 tokens showed as 105% on a seat Claude Code was
compacting natively at 240k. A served id the family does not catalogue reads
the family default, as the launch line does.

**A live seat the watchdog cannot measure says UNKNOWN.** Every rung above
starts from a percentage, so a seat with no window or no reading could never
be seen by any of them. When the census says the seat is live (or cannot look,
and the seat holds a registered pane) and one of these holds for 10 minutes,
one line names the seat and why, once per episode:

- `UNKNOWN window`: the family pins no window and the assumed window is off.
- `UNKNOWN context`: no session transcript under the seat's
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, a transcript with no non-zero usage record, a reading
  with no age, or a registered session with no transcript there while an older
  one of another session is newest.

A seat with no live process stays quiet, and an idle seat whose old transcript
is its registered session is measured, not unknown. `--json` carries the rows
as `unknown`; each row carries `unmeasured` and `unmeasured_why`.

`--dry-run` reports decisions without injecting or latching; `--seat S` limits
the pass; `--threshold N`, `--json`, and `--quiet` shape it. `--install-timer
[--interval SEC] --apply` installs the external systemd user cadence (60s by
default). `seat launch`, `seat spawn`, and `seat resume` refresh and enable that
timer automatically; a system without systemd gets a warning and can schedule
the same bounded command another way.

Claude-model seats are scanned too. The old skip ("native seats autocompact
fine") was right only about CC's *native* autocompaction, which continues the
turn it interrupts; deliberate self-compaction at 80% is what the owner wants
for every helm agent, and it is safe only behind the resume leg below.
`HELM_AUTOCOMPACT_CLAUDE=0` restores the skip for a fleet that has not
installed that hook.

**`helm seat resume-turn --hook-json` — the RESUME leg of a compaction.**
A compaction ends a turn and nothing starts the next one, so before this
existed a seat compacted and then slept until a human typed into its pane
(bug class `compaction-has-no-resume-leg`: `autocompact` fired correctly, the
PreCompact handoff hook wrote correctly, and jointly they parked the seat).
Wired as a `SessionStart` hook on every home and every seat, it acts **only**
when the payload's `source` is `compact`.

**Two kinds of compaction arrive with that source, and only the deliberate
one needs the leg.** Claude Code's own native autocompaction continues the
interrupted turn by itself; a `/compact` typed by a human or injected by
`autocompact` ends the turn and parks the seat. The SessionStart payload
cannot tell them apart — the distinction is the `trigger` field of the
PreCompact payload one hook earlier (`auto` / `manual`), which `helm handoff
check --hook-json` records under the session's key in the resume-turn state.
This leg reads that record: a recent `auto` (inside
`HELM_RESUME_TURN_SPIRAL_S`, which covers the 100–190s a compaction takes and
sits far under the hours between two compactions of one session), written by
the same thread (the record's `agent` equals the payload's `agent_id`; a
subagent shares the seat's key and its record vouches only for a subagent)
and not yet consumed, means nothing is injected, no room row is posted and no
DM is sent; the decision leaves one stderr line, a `native-auto` entry in
`--status`, and a `seat.resume-turn` ledger event. One record vouches for
exactly one SessionStart: the decision marks it consumed in the same locked
write. A record with a present-invalid field — a null record, a non-finite or
non-numeric `at`, a missing or mistyped `trigger`, `session` or `agent` —
never vouches, and a record stamped at or before the entry's last recorded
resume-turn decision (`last_at`, which every decision stamps) is obsolete and
never vouches. And the record is BOUND TO A TRANSCRIPT POSITION: the
PreCompact recorded the transcript's byte length, inode and device, and this
leg vouches only when the file it OPENS at the payload's `transcript_path` is
the same inode and device, has not shrunk, has grown by at most
`resumeturn.TRANSCRIPT_GROWTH_CAP`
(4 MiB, a read bound sized over six times the largest same-compaction growth
measured), and nothing appended since the recorded position is a
`compact_boundary` record (the record's compaction already ended — its
boundary and summary are on disk, and a stale record read by a later
compaction's SessionStart is exactly this) or a `user`/`assistant` turn (it
never ended and the session moved on). ONE DESCRIPTOR IS MEASURED AND READ:
the path is opened once, nonblocking and regular-only (`pk.open_regular`),
`os.fstat` of THAT descriptor gives the identity and the size the interval is
computed from, and the read must return the WHOLE interval — a file replaced
or truncated between a pathname stat and a separate open handed the old shape
an empty region, and an empty region holds no boundary and no turn, so a stale
record vouched over it. The read also happens BEFORE the state lock is taken
and its result is an input to the locked decision, so a FIFO or a slow file at
the transcript path can never hold the store's lock against the fallback leg;
the cap bounds the BYTES, and the nonblocking regular-only open prevents a
FIFO-open hang, not slow regular-file I/O. Observation exceptions, including
malformed paths and close failures, decline native-auto inside the same fallback
boundary as consumption failures; observation still happens outside the lock.
Past a declined record the ACT has one boundary of its own: composing the
directive (`resume_text`, which opens the transcript for the compaction
floor), writing it and forking the child fail into the same alert — a wake
child carrying the error, the stderr line — never into the hook's last-resort
catch, which prints and returns 0 with nothing armed. A transcript path the
kernel refuses (an embedded NUL raises ValueError, not OSError) reached that
catch once under a matching register: native-auto declined
loudly, the register matched, and the leg died silently between the decision
and the spawn. The PreCompact producer refuses the same path the same way
(`_transcript_position`: no position, one stderr line), so the record stays
written and the nag still runs.
Measured on 431 boundaries: the
harness creates the boundary AFTER this hook has finished on every build
from 2.1.204 on and writes the summary after the boundary, so neither is on
disk while the leg runs, and what does land in between is session metadata
and queued messages, never a turn. Every failure to PROVE the binding — no
`transcript_path` in either payload, a record without a position, a file
that cannot be read, a path that is not a regular file, a replaced inode, a
shrunk file, growth past the cap, a read shorter than the interval,
an unparseable record in the region — declines with one stderr line naming
which, and declining is the loud path. A `manual` record, a consumed,
obsolete or unbound one, a subagent's, an unrecognised trigger, or no record
at all is the resume leg described below, byte for byte — absence of the
record is not proof of a native compaction (the PreCompact hook may be
uninstalled, timed out, or given up on the state lock inside its bound), and
the loud path is the one whose cost is a spurious row rather than a parked
seat. BOUNDARY, what remains: a binding is unprovable when the transcript is
unreadable on both sides (the producer could not stat it, or this leg
cannot), and unprovable declines — one spurious resume alert over a native
compaction, never a silent parked seat. Measured before this: 240 "could NOT
be auto-resumed" rows (~85 KB) in one room, every one about a seat that had
already resumed on its own.

The hook itself never touches the pane — a `SessionStart` hook runs *before*
the session resumes, so an inline injection lands ahead of the composer.
It does file reads only, then forks a **detached child** that waits out the
composer settle (`HELM_RESUME_TURN_SETTLE_S`, default 3s — measured against a
real Claude Code TUI on a pty) and injects through the metaharness seam,
re-proving pane identity inside the seat lifecycle lock at send time. The
directive is the seat's **own** freshest handoff entry (`NEXT:`), so it resumes
on real work rather than a generic "continue"; with no handoff written for that
compaction it injects a re-ground line instead. A pane that cannot be
authoritatively identified is never guessed at: it gets a loud chat alert
naming the seat.

The loop guard makes compact→resume→compact impossible by construction: a
second `SessionStart(compact)` within `HELM_RESUME_TURN_DEBOUNCE_S` is the same
episode re-firing (silent no-op); a genuinely new compaction within
`HELM_RESUME_TURN_SPIRAL_S` of a resume stops injecting and alerts; and
`HELM_RESUME_TURN_MAX` resumes per rolling `HELM_RESUME_TURN_WINDOW_S` caps the
slow case. Those three answers are read from the resume-turn state store,
and a store that exists and cannot be read answers none of them: the hook
injects nothing, alerts the room with no DM, prints the `unknown` refusal and
its reason on its own SessionStart output (the one line the compacted seat
reads, as it does for spiral and capped), and the same refusal governs the
deaf-in-effect nudge and the episode wake DM, until the store is repaired or
moved aside (`helm doctor` FAILs naming it). `helm seat resume-turn --status`
prints what the leg last did per seat, or that the store is UNREADABLE;
`HELM_RESUME_TURN=0` disarms it.

**A proxy seat cannot fan out through a skill or a fork — the deny set, not
the brief.** Every seat launches without plan-mode ENTRY; a seat on a **proxy
family** (codex, kimi, gemini, grok, ds4pro — each request spends a metered
upstream quota) also launches without `Skill` and `Agent(fork)`. The set lives
in one place, `seat_catalog.denied_tools(family)`, and rides three surfaces:
the launch line's `--disallowedTools`, the seat config dir's
`permissions.deny` (what a resume or an Orca relaunch inherits), and the
`disallowedTools` frontmatter of every subagent definition `seat launch
--multi` / `seat smoke` mints. The reason is an incident class, not a
preference: one run emptied two codex quotas through the skill door
(task/2287, 437 subagents and 32 forks). A brief binds the model's own `Agent`
calls; it cannot bind the agents a skill launches for itself, so the bound
must be mechanical. A native claude seat keeps both tools, and a slash command
the OWNER types in a pane is a different path and still works.

**A proxy seat MAY run a workflow — capped, and on its own tier.** `Workflow`
was denied on proxy seats too after a briefed reader reached 14 concurrent
agents through a workflow script (task/2491); the owner's ruling reversed that
half (task/2559): "astra can run sol workflows just like fable can run opus
workflows ... both valid strategies for cross-model same-family delegation
within a cc process, so the policy needs to be more nuanced". So the tool
stays, and the bound is mechanical in two parts. **The cap**: every proxy
launch line that keeps the tool (all but a lite family that denies it, see
"The lite launch profile") exports
`CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS=4` (the one
workflow knob the harness reads, per workflow run; the seat's settings.json
`env` map carries the same key so a resume inherits it), where the harness
default is 16. It bounds one run — two workflows in flight may hold eight —
and the seat-wide subagent ceiling is unchanged. **The tier**: a workflow
agent's `model` is sent upstream as a claude id, exactly like a built-in agent
type's frontmatter, so the seat's `oauth-model-alias` block (below) decides
where it lands: on a codex seat every id runs `gpt-6.1-sol`, and an agent that
names no model inherits the pane's. The admission is
the owner ruling recorded on helm task/2559 (origin: owner), in the owner's
words: "astra can run sol workflows just like fable can run opus workflows,
same diff, both valid strategies for cross-model same-family delegation within
a cc process, well then the policy needs to be more nuanced, report to helm
team for fixing"; its scope is every proxy-family seat run inside the Claude
Code harness (the `seat_catalog` proxy modes), native claude seats outside
it. The ruling admits the tool; it does not itself speak of pre-existing deny
entries, and the old seeder's documented contract preserved every entry it
found, so an upgraded seat's settings.json is handled by three explicit legs
(`seat_catalog.RETIRED_SPAWN_DENIES`), none of which reads a list's shape or
a file's location as proof of who wrote an entry. **Recorded by the
operator**: an entry under `helm.operator_denies` is a helm-honoured key the
refresh never edits and always re-applies to `permissions.deny` — an operator
who wants `Workflow` denied on a proxy seat records it there. A family on
the lite launch profile with no same-family delegate tier denies `Workflow`
again by its own rule (see "The lite launch profile" above), so nothing
retires it there. **Recorded by
helm**: every seed records what helm itself wrote under `helm.seeded_denies`
(the seeder is the only writer; census and doctor may read it); a retired
entry that record names is removed with its record, and the record never
names an entry the list no longer carries. **Unrecorded**: left untouched,
`Workflow` included — no automatic path removes it, in or out of helm's own
tree — and the refresh prints one line naming the entry, the file, and the
verb below. A native claude seat is not a proxy family: nothing is removed
there.

### `helm seat retire-deny <tool> [--seat S|--all] [--apply]`

The deliberate door for the unrecorded case. Dry-run by default, and the dry
run IS the list: every proxy-seat settings.json (the family dir and each
instance dir) carrying a deny of `<tool>` that neither `helm.seeded_denies`
nor `helm.operator_denies` records, marked `WOULD-REMOVE`; an entry the
operator key names is listed `KEPT`, one helm's record names `HELM-OWNED`
(the next refresh retires it). Every candidate is judged before anything is
written, and three states block every write and exit 1: `REFUSED` — the
candidate's instance dir or its `claude` child resolves to another seat's
tree (the seeder's own identity and nesting guards, applied before any
read, so a linked directory can never carry a write into the seat it points
at); `UNREADABLE` — the strict reader failed (a dangling link, a FIFO, a
directory helm cannot enter), named with its errno and never silently
absent; `MALFORMED` — the file's root or a present `permissions` container
is not an object (a file of `null` is a value, never a missing file; a
`"permissions": "Workflow"` is never read as no deny), or `permissions.deny`,
`helm.seeded_denies` or `helm.operator_denies` is not a list of strings —
none of which is ever read as permission to remove, and none of which is
ever read as absent. `--apply` then removes exactly the named entry from
exactly the `WOULD-REMOVE` files, appends nothing to `helm.seeded_denies`
(the entry is gone), prints one `REMOVED` line per file, never touches an
entry `helm.operator_denies` names and never touches a non-proxy seat; a
second `--apply` lists nothing and writes nothing. It refuses a tool the
current table still denies (a refresh would seed it straight back). A tool
only a launch profile denies (`Workflow` on a lite family) is not refused:
that profile's families are left out of the sweep, and `--seat` of one of
them is refused. **Applying it fleet-wide is an owner
decision** — it is not authorized by a review or by the integrator, and
nothing in deploy or doctor runs it.
Not mechanical: a
script that names an upstream id verbatim (`gpt-6-astra`) is served as
written, because the alias rows keep the family's real ids routable on
purpose. A native claude seat carries no cap; its workflows are the owner's.

### `helm seat remint <seat>|--all [--apply] [--follow-catalog|--keep-persisted]`

**A seat's launch.sh never silently runs a model the catalog, or the seat's
explicit choice, does not name.** launch.sh is re-minted only by `add`,
`launch`, `spawn` and `resume`, so a catalog change reaches a seat only when
one of those runs. On 2026-09-28 the gemini seat's script, three days old,
still said `gemini-3.6-flash-high` while the catalog, its proxy config and
its settings.json said 3.8; started from that script, the seat came up on a
route with no credential and stayed dead until the owner typed `/model` by
hand.

`helm seat doctor` asks, per minted seat with a launch.sh, what a FRESH MINT
would write now (the model, the subagent pin and every environment word of
the launch line, rendered by `launch_line` from the room and `--multi` shape
the script already carries) and prints one `launch drift: <seat> DRIFT` row
per seat whose script differs, naming each field `old -> new` and where the
new model comes from (`catalog`, `explicit choice`). A DRIFT row fails the
doctor's exit status; a launch.sh or spawn.json helm cannot read (or a
spawn.json that is not an object) prints `UNKNOWN` and does not, because a
choice helm could not read is not an absent one. The room is compared as the
seat reads it: `HELM_CHAT_ROOM_SOURCE=explicit` beside a room, which a
`--room` spawn stamps, reads the same as no stamp, so a fresh spawn is never
DRIFT.

`helm seat remint` is the cure, for one seat or `--all`. Dry run by default,
and the dry run IS the plan: the same fields, the launch.sh it would rewrite
and the proxy config it would regenerate. `--apply` re-mints through the
refresh `launch` and `resume` already run and regenerates the proxy config
through the path `doctor --ensure` uses, under the seat's lifecycle lock. It
refuses, writing nothing, on an UNKNOWN row and while another spawn's PENDING
attempt owns the seat (the `IN FLIGHT` door every mutating verb asks first). It
never starts or stops a process: a running pane keeps its model. Nothing is
launched, so the re-minted launch.sh no longer states the launch the pane ran:
a plain `helm seat resume <seat>` brings the seat back on the recipe it ran
with only from its own process or a capture of it (task/3695), and refuses a
recipe that mixes the transcript with launch.sh; the re-minted launch reaches
it through `helm seat resume <seat> --defaults`. A running proxy takes the new
config at its next `seat up` or ensure pass. It writes nothing outside the
seat's own directory.

**A default is not a choice.** spawn.json records `model_source` beside a
persisted model: `explicit` (the operator's `--model`, which outranks the
catalog on every re-mint) or `default` (the family model at that moment,
kept as history, which the catalog outranks). A record written before the
marker existed cannot say which it was — helm keeps no history of what the
catalog said then — so its model is KEPT, as it always was, and wherever it
differs from the catalog the row says `persisted, source unknown` and counts
as DRIFT until the operator decides: `--follow-catalog --apply` records it as
the default (the seat follows the catalog from then on), `--keep-persisted
--apply` records it as a choice. That decision is the only spawn.json write
this verb makes.

### `helm router [up|run|down|status|line|probes]` + `helm seat launch|smoke --multi`

**Mixed models in ONE claude-code process** (proven 2026-07-21, raw conductor
logs): a Task subagent's `.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter `model:` string
goes to the wire per-request, and the proxy routes each request by model
name. The one law: **never set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` for a mixed
fleet** — it blunt-pins every subagent over the frontmatter. Two surfaces:

- **`helm seat launch <family> --multi`** — the proxied-parent shape (e.g.
  codex parent + mixed codex subagents): the launch line drops the
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` pin and probe agents (per-model frontmatter)
  are minted into the seat's config dir. `helm seat smoke <family> --multi`
  adds the mixed fan-out leg: two subagents pinned to different models
  through an ephemeral router, PASS only when the router's **conductor log**
  shows both models on the wire (never the subagents' word).
- **`helm router`** — the claude-PARENT shape. `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is
  process-global, so a Claude parent with non-claude subagents needs one
  local endpoint speaking both worlds: the router forwards `claude-*`
  requests **verbatim** to api.anthropic.com (claude-code's own OAuth
  Authorization header, body, and headers untouched — no substitution, no
  re-auth, and NEVER an Anthropic API key), and conducts non-claude models
  to their seat's CLIProxyAPI with the seat token. `helm router line` prints
  the parent launch line (`env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
  -u CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8320
  claude`); `helm router probes` mints the example per-model agents into a
  project's `.claude/agents/`. Every request appends one paste-safe JSON
  line (model/route/status — never header values) to
  `~/.helm/_global/router/router.log`: the conductor log.

**A SUBAGENT'S MODEL IS ITS FRONTMATTER ID, AND THE FAMILY DECIDES WHERE THAT
ID GOES.** CC's built-in agent types carry a claude model in their own
frontmatter and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` does not override it (measured
2026-09-09: an Explore child on an astra seat sent `claude-opus-5` upstream and
died HTTP 502), so every proxy seat's config carries an `oauth-model-alias`
block mapping each catalogued frontmatter id onto a model the family serves.
By default that is **the seat's own launch model** — one pane, one model,
nothing to choose. A family that declares a **`subagent_tiers`** table in
`helm/seat_catalog.py` names a model **per id** instead, and codex declares
one: `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and the undated
`claude-haiku-4-5` (what CC's own alias table resolves the word `haiku` to)
-> `gpt-6.1-sol`, while `claude-opus-5`, `claude-opus-5-5` and
`claude-fable-5-1` carry no row and therefore follow the seat's launch model,
which is also `gpt-6.1-sol`. So every codex subagent runs `gpt-6.1-sol`.
The worker rows stay declared so that a pane an operator pinned to another
model with `--model` still sends its workers to `gpt-6.1-sol`; its checkers run
what the pane runs. Every tier value must be a model
that family catalogues (its `model`, a `probe_models` entry, or a
`model_context` key) or the catalog refuses to import; a family with no table
emits its launch model on every row, byte-identical to before (kimi,
gemini, grok). `helm seat doctor --ensure` reconciles a live config to the
block the generator now emits, so declaring a tier respawns that family's
sidecars on the next sweep. One caveat with no knob behind it:
`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` is process-global, so every subagent believes
the PANE's window, and the invariant that keeps that safe is **the advertised
window must be no larger than the capacity of EVERY model this family routes a
child to**. A child WIDER than its pane is UNDERSTATED, which compacts early
rather than wedging — the safe direction. The dangerous direction is a NARROWER
child than the pane: a pane told 320000 with a tier at 220000 overstates those
children by 100k, the unrecoverable direction, and a tier on a model narrower
than the launch model is what would force the launch line to advertise the
MINIMUM over the launch model and every tier model. Every codex seat launches
on `gpt-6.1-sol` (220000) and its tiers are `gpt-6.1-sol` (220000).
No shipped tier is narrower than its pane. The one pane that breaks it is one
an operator pinned to gpt-5.6-sol with `--model` (told 320000, workers on
`gpt-6.1-sol`'s 220000): relaunch such a pane on `gpt-6.1-sol` rather than
keep it.

**AN INSTANCE MAY DECLARE ITS OWN LAUNCH MODEL, SO ONE FAMILY CAN SPAN TWO.**
`FAMILIES[...]["instance_models"]` names a model **per instance**: one family
entry, one OAuth cred pool, two models across panes. Codex once used the table
to split instances across gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-6-astra; the family model is now
`gpt-6.1-sol` and every codex instance launches on it, so no shipped family
declares a table. An instance with no row launches on the family model, so
every family without a table mints the config and launch line it minted
before. Each key must be an instance of that family (`codex` or
`codex-<N>`) and each value a model the family catalogues, or the catalog
refuses to import — the same `family_catalogued_models` reading the tier
validator uses. The declaration reaches the seat through the generator, not
through a file on disk: `helm seat doctor --ensure` regenerates every instance
config from it (a hand edit is reverted within the minute), the launch line
carries the instance model plus that model's `model_context` window (a
gpt-5.6-sol pane is told 320000, a gpt-6.1-sol pane 220000), and `helm seat
list` prints TWO model columns per seat: `declared` (the catalog default) beside `minted` (the model
that seat's own launch.sh on disk would spawn, `unminted` where no launch.sh
exists, `UNKNOWN` where helm could not answer from that path — the read's error
class is printed beside it). There is no `launched` column: launch.sh is
re-minted on every add, launch and resume, so it proves what the NEXT spawn
uses and not what the live pane started with, and the only record a pane
self-writes (the roster runtime row) carries harness, family and backend and
no model at all. An explicit `helm seat launch <seat> --model`
still outranks the declaration for that pane. A seat whose launch.sh on disk
names another model than that answer reads `DRIFT` in `helm seat doctor`, and
`helm seat remint` re-mints it (below).
